# Checkout

Fetches all unread GitHub notifications and presents them as a prioritised, scannable inbox — without opening a browser.

Usage: `/checkout`

---

## Step 1 — Fetch all unread notifications

```bash
gh api /notifications?all=false&per_page=100 --paginate
```

This returns all unread notifications across every repo you have access to.

---

## Step 2 — Convert API URLs to web URLs

Each notification's `subject.url` is an API URL. Convert to a human-usable web URL:

- `https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo/pulls/123` → `https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123`
- `https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo/issues/123` → `https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123`
- `https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo/releases/123` → `https://github.com/owner/repo/releases/tag/...` (use `repository.html_url/releases`)
- For anything else: use `https://github.com/<repository.full_name>`

---

## Step 3 — Classify and prioritise

Use the `reason` field to assign a priority tier:

**🔴 Needs your action**
- `review_requested` — someone asked you to review a PR
- `mention` — you were @mentioned
- `team_mention` — your team was @mentioned
- `assign` — you were assigned to an issue or PR
- `security_alert` — security vulnerability detected

**🟡 FYI / follow-up**
- `comment` — new comment on something you're involved in
- `state_change` — issue or PR you follow changed state (closed, merged…)
- `author` — activity on something you created

**⚪ Low priority (subscribed noise)**
- `subscribed` — activity on a repo you watch
- `manual` — something you manually subscribed to
- `your_activity` — triggered by your own actions

---

## Step 4 — Output the inbox

Group by priority tier, then by repo within each tier. Format:

```
🔴 Needs your action (N)

  wp-media/backwpup-pro
  · [review requested] Fix backup destination timeout — PR #512
    https://github.com/wp-media/backwpup-pro/pull/512

  wp-media/backwpup-pro
  · [mention] Question about the S3 handler — Issue #498
    https://github.com/wp-media/backwpup-pro/issues/498

🟡 FYI / follow-up (N)

  owner/repo
  · [comment] CI is failing on main — PR #201
    https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/201

⚪ Low priority (N) — skipped for brevity
```

Rules:
- Always show 🔴 and 🟡 in full
- For ⚪, just print the count and skip the list (noise reduction)
- If 🔴 is empty, say so explicitly: "Nothing urgent 🎉"
- Keep titles to one line — truncate at 80 chars if needed
- Sort within each group by `updated_at` descending (most recent first)
- Do NOT mark notifications as read — leave that to the user

name: checkout
description: List all your unread GitHub notifications, grouped by priority and type (mention, review requested, assigned, etc.) with clickable URLs. Use this as a quick daily triage of everything waiting for your attention on GitHub — like checking github.com/notifications but from the terminal. Invoke with `/checkout`.
---

# Checkout

Fetches all unread GitHub notifications and presents them as a prioritised, scannable inbox — without opening a browser.

Usage: `/checkout`

---

## Step 1 — Fetch all unread notifications

```bash
gh api /notifications?all=false&per_page=100 --paginate
```

This returns all unread notifications across every repo you have access to.

---

## Step 2 — Convert API URLs to web URLs

Each notification's `subject.url` is an API URL. Convert to a human-usable web URL:

- `https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo/pulls/123` → `https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123`
- `https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo/issues/123` → `https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123`
- `https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo/releases/123` → `https://github.com/owner/repo/releases/tag/...` (use `repository.html_url/releases`)
- For anything else: use `https://github.com/<repository.full_name>`

---

## Step 3 — Classify and prioritise

Use the `reason` field to assign a priority tier:

**🔴 Needs your action**
- `review_requested` — someone asked you to review a PR
- `mention` — you were @mentioned
- `team_mention` — your team was @mentioned
- `assign` — you were assigned to an issue or PR
- `security_alert` — security vulnerability detected

**🟡 FYI / follow-up**
- `comment` — new comment on something you're involved in
- `state_change` — issue or PR you follow changed state (closed, merged…)
- `author` — activity on something you created

**⚪ Low priority (subscribed noise)**
- `subscribed` — activity on a repo you watch
- `manual` — something you manually subscribed to
- `your_activity` — triggered by your own actions

---

## Step 4 — Output the inbox

Group by priority tier, then by repo within each tier. Format:

```
🔴 Needs your action (N)

  wp-media/backwpup-pro
  · [review requested] Fix backup destination timeout — PR #512
    https://github.com/wp-media/backwpup-pro/pull/512

  wp-media/backwpup-pro
  · [mention] Question about the S3 handler — Issue #498
    https://github.com/wp-media/backwpup-pro/issues/498

🟡 FYI / follow-up (N)

  owner/repo
  · [comment] CI is failing on main — PR #201
    https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/201

⚪ Low priority (N) — skipped for brevity
```

Rules:
- Always show 🔴 and 🟡 in full
- For ⚪, just print the count and skip the list (noise reduction)
- If 🔴 is empty, say so explicitly: "Nothing urgent 🎉"
- Keep titles to one line — truncate at 80 chars if needed
- Sort within each group by `updated_at` descending (most recent first)
- Do NOT mark notifications as read — leave that to the user

# Checkout

Fetches all unread GitHub notifications and presents them as a prioritised, scannable inbox — without opening a browser.

Usage: `/checkout`

---

## Step 1 — Fetch all unread notifications

```bash
gh api /notifications?all=false&per_page=100 --paginate
```

This returns all unread notifications across every repo you have access to.

---

## Step 2 — Convert API URLs to web URLs

Each notification's `subject.url` is an API URL. Convert to a human-usable web URL:

- `https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo/pulls/123` → `https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123`
- `https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo/issues/123` → `https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123`
- `https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo/releases/123` → `https://github.com/owner/repo/releases/tag/...` (use `repository.html_url/releases`)
- For anything else: use `https://github.com/<repository.full_name>`

---

## Step 3 — Classify and prioritise

Use the `reason` field to assign a priority tier:

**🔴 Needs your action**
- `review_requested` — someone asked you to review a PR
- `mention` — you were @mentioned
- `team_mention` — your team was @mentioned
- `assign` — you were assigned to an issue or PR
- `security_alert` — security vulnerability detected

**🟡 FYI / follow-up**
- `comment` — new comment on something you're involved in
- `state_change` — issue or PR you follow changed state (closed, merged…)
- `author` — activity on something you created

**⚪ Low priority (subscribed noise)**
- `subscribed` — activity on a repo you watch
- `manual` — something you manually subscribed to
- `your_activity` — triggered by your own actions

---

## Step 4 — Output the inbox

### Header

Open with a one-line summary banner, then a blank line:

```
📬 **GitHub Inbox** — {Day D Month YYYY} · 🔴 {N} urgent · 🟡 {N} fyi · ⚪ {N} noise
```

---

### Priority tiers

Render each tier as a markdown section. Within each tier, group by repo (bold heading + item count). Each notification is **one line**: an emoji icon, a markdown hyperlink title, and a compact age label.

**Tier headings:**
- `### 🔴 Needs your action (N)`
- `### 🟡 FYI / follow-up (N)`
- `### ⚪ Low priority — N items skipped`

**Per-repo heading:**  `**owner/repo** · N`

**Per-item format** (one line, no bare URL):
```
- {icon} [{Title truncated to 72 chars}]({web_url}) `{label}` · *{age}*
```

**Icon map:**

| reason | icon |
|--------|------|
| `assign` | 👤 |
| `review_requested` | 👁 |
| `mention` | 💬 |
| `team_mention` | 📢 |
| `security_alert` | 🚨 |
| `comment` | 💭 |
| `state_change` | 🔄 |
| `author` | ✍️ |

**Label:** short human string — `PR #123`, `Issue #456`, or `Release`

**Age:** relative to today — `today`, `yesterday`, `Mon`, `May 22`, `Mar 4`. Never show the year unless it's a different year.

**Example output:**

```

### ⚪ Low priority — 3 items skipped

### Rules

- Never print bare URLs — every link must be a markdown hyperlink `[text](url)`
- Always show 🔴 and 🟡 in full
- For ⚪: one-liner count only, no listing

- Sort within each group by `updated_at` descending (most recent first)

# Checkout

Fetches all unread GitHub notifications and presents them as a prioritised, scannable inbox — without opening a browser.

Usage: `/checkout`

---

## Step 1 — Fetch all unread notifications

```bash
gh api /notifications?all=false&per_page=100 --paginate
```

This returns all unread notifications across every repo you have access to.

---

## Step 1.5 — Filter to last 7 days

After fetching, filter out notifications older than 7 days using `updated_at`. Use the current date (today) to calculate. Discard anything from before 7 days ago.

---

## Step 2 — Convert API URLs to web URLs

Each notification's `subject.url` is an API URL. Convert to a human-usable web URL:

- `https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo/pulls/123` → `https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123`
- `https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo/issues/123` → `https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123`
- `https://api.github.com/repos/owner/repo/releases/123` → `https://github.com/owner/repo/releases/tag/...` (use `repository.html_url/releases`)
- For anything else: use `https://github.com/<repository.full_name>`

---

## Step 3 — Classify and prioritise

Use the `reason` field to assign a priority tier:

**🔴 Needs your action**
- `review_requested` — someone asked you to review a PR
- `mention` — you were @mentioned
- `team_mention` — your team was @mentioned
- `assign` — you were assigned to an issue or PR
- `security_alert` — security vulnerability detected

**🟡 FYI / follow-up**
- `comment` — new comment on something you're involved in
- `state_change` — issue or PR you follow changed state (closed, merged…)
- `author` — activity on something you created

**⚪ Low priority (subscribed noise)**
- `subscribed` — activity on a repo you watch
- `manual` — something you manually subscribed to
- `your_activity` — triggered by your own actions

---

## Step 4 — Output the inbox

### Header

Open with a one-line summary banner, then a blank line:

```
📬 **GitHub Inbox** — {Day D Month YYYY} · 🔴 {N} urgent · 🟡 {N} fyi · ⚪ {N} noise
```

---

### Priority tiers

Render each tier as a markdown section. Within each tier, group by repo (bold heading + item count). Each notification is **one line**: an emoji icon, a markdown hyperlink title, and a compact age label.

**Tier headings:**
- `### 🔴 Needs your action (N)`
- `### 🟡 FYI / follow-up (N)`
- `### ⚪ Low priority — N items skipped`

**Per-repo heading:**  `**owner/repo** · N`

**Per-item format** (one line, no bare URL):
```
- {icon} [{Title truncated to 72 chars}]({web_url}) `{label}` · *{age}*
```

**Icon map:**

| reason | icon |
|--------|------|
| `assign` | 👤 |
| `review_requested` | 👁 |
| `mention` | 💬 |
| `team_mention` | 📢 |
| `security_alert` | 🚨 |
| `comment` | 💭 |
| `state_change` | 🔄 |
| `author` | ✍️ |

**Label:** short human string — `PR #123`, `Issue #456`, or `Release`

**Age:** relative to today — `today`, `yesterday`, `Mon`, `May 22`, `Mar 4`. Never show the year unless it's a different year.

**Example output:**

```
📬 **GitHub Inbox** — Tuesday 3 June 2026 · 🔴 12 urgent · 🟡 8 fyi · ⚪ 3 noise

### 🔴 Needs your action (12)

**wp-media/backwpup-pro** · 5

- 💬 [[NUDGE] Main issue for the Nudge feature](https://github.com/wp-media/backwpup-pro/issues/1617) `Issue #1617` · *May 22*

**wp-media/wp-rocket** · 7
- 👤 [Closes #8353: Surface Rocket Insights URL validation errors](https://github.com/wp-media/wp-rocket/pull/8376) `PR #8376` · *Mon*
- 👁 [Fix #2698: Prevent unnecessary cache purges for hierarchical pages](https://github.com/wp-media/wp-rocket/pull/7613) `PR #7613` · *Apr 7*

### 🟡 FYI / follow-up (8)

**wp-media/backwpup-pro** · 3
- 💭 [Backup creation might get stuck around 55% on large websites](https://github.com/wp-media/backwpup-pro/issues/570) `Issue #570` · *May 20*
- 🔄 [WP Super Cache gets disabled when BackWPup job starts](https://github.com/wp-media/backwpup-pro/pull/1658) `PR #1658` · *May 21*

### ⚪ Low priority — 3 items skipped
```

---

### Rules

- Never print bare URLs — every link must be a markdown hyperlink `[text](url)`
- Always show 🔴 and 🟡 in full
- For ⚪: one-liner count only, no listing
- If 🔴 is empty: replace the section with `### 🔴 Nothing urgent 🎉`
- Sort within each group by `updated_at` descending (most recent first)
- Truncate titles at 72 chars with `…` if needed
- Do NOT mark notifications as read — leave that to the user
